message:
feat(update): embed the operational public key, and stop asserting there is none

The key is raw X||Y, 128 hex characters, on both platforms. Not the SPKI
form: that decodes cleanly and then fails a length check inside the
verifier, so every update would be refused with no error anywhere and the
build would look exactly like one with nothing published. Both suites now
assert the length and the alphabet, and that it is not 182 characters.

Two assertions had to change with it. They said the trusted key was empty,
which was true of a temporary state; keeping them would mean asserting the
product cannot check updates. They assert the same safety property from the
other side now -- the shipped key must refuse a document signed by any other
key, and the shared test vectors are signed by exactly such a key.

The C++ suite also learned to tell which fixture it is looking at. Run
against the shared vectors it requires a refusal; run against a fixture
signed by the release key it requires acceptance and then a refusal once one
byte moves. Asserting only the refusal would have left "can this key verify
anything at all" untested, and a verifier that refuses everything passes a
refusal test perfectly.

Found while doing it: Android had two answers to "which key do we trust".
UpdateManifest.trustedPublicKeyHex() returned a hard-coded empty string
while the value the app actually verifies with came from BuildConfig -- so
the tests asked one and the product used the other. Embedding the key made
them disagree, which is how it surfaced. It delegates to BuildConfig now.
